None of these gave ethyl acetate. Perhaps the target molecule is not ethyl acrylate. The precursor we got earlier is CCOC(=O)C (ethyl acetate). That suggests the product might be something like "C=CC(=O)OCC" (ethyl acrylate) but applying template gave ethyl acetate as one of the fragments? Not.

Maybe the product is a β-keto ester? Let's think: Still-Gennari reaction forms Z-alkene between aldehyde carbonyl carbon and phosphonate carbon, giving an α,β-unsaturated ester. The phosphonate ester is diethyl phosphonoacetate (EtO)2P(=O)CH2CO2Et. After reaction, the product is an α,β-unsaturated ester (R-CH=CH-CO2Et). The byproduct is a phosphonate (EtO)2P(=O)O-? Not ethyl acetate. So maybe the precursor list includes the phosphonate component after conversion to ethyl acetate? Not.

Maybe the target molecule is "CCOC(=O)C=CHC(=O)O" (ethyl 3-oxoprop-2-enoate) which when broken yields ethyl acetate (CCOC(=O)C) and something else (maybe aldehyde). Let's test apply_template with product "CCOC(=O)C=CC(=O)O"? That's ethyl 3-oxoprop-2-enoate (maybe). Use template 247363 again.
